items.text: Morgan Stanley states that for certain revenue-producing employees in the Wealth Management and Investment Management business segments, compensation is largely paid on the basis of formulaic payouts that link employee compensation to revenues.
items.quote: For certain revenue-producing employees in the Wealth Management and Investment Management business segments, compensation is largely paid on the basis of formulaic payouts that link employee compensation to revenues.
items.scope: Wealth Management and Investment Management business segments

items.text: Morgan Stanley attributes the increase in 2025 compensation and benefits expenses to an increase in the formulaic payout to Wealth Management advisors, implying a formulaic payout structure tied to revenues.
items.quote: primarily due to an increase in the formulaic payout to Wealth Management advisors and higher discretionary incentive compensation within Institutional Securities, both on higher revenues, and higher salary expenses.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states that the amount of the advisory fee a client pays is a factor used in calculating the compensation paid to the Financial Advisor, and that if the fee rate is below a certain threshold, the Financial Advisor receives credit for less than the total amount of the fee in calculating compensation; Financial Advisors therefore have a financial incentive not to reduce fees.
items.quote: The amount of the fee you pay is a factor we use in calculating the compensation we pay your Financial Advisor... If your fee rate is below a certain threshold, we give your Financial Advisor credit for less than the total amount of your fee in calculating his or her compensation.

items.text: Morgan Stanley discloses that a Morgan Stanley Virtual Advisor (MSVA) is paid a base salary plus a discretionary bonus and does not retain any portion of the Morgan Stanley Advisory Fee.
items.quote: If your account is serviced through a Morgan Stanley Virtual Advisor ("MSVA"), your MSVA is paid a base salary plus a discretionary bonus and does not retain any portion of the Morgan Stanley Advisory Fee.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states it will increase the cash component of its advisor compensation to reduce accounting-driven volatility and simplify its compensation program.
items.quote: we will also increase the cash component of our advisor compensation. We are making these changes to reduce the accounting-driven volatility in revenues and earnings... will help simplify our compensation program.

items.text: Morgan Stanley defines how compensation expense for deferred cash-based compensation plans (DCP) awards is calculated: based on the notional value of the award granted, adjusted for changes in fair value of referenced investments employees select, and recognized over the vesting period.
items.quote: Compensation expense for deferred cash-based compensation plans awards is calculated based on the notional value of the award granted, adjusted for changes in the fair value of the referenced investments that employees select. Compensation expense is recognized over the vesting period relevant to each separately vesting portion of deferred awards.
items.definition: Compensation expense for deferred cash-based compensation plans awards is calculated based on the notional value of the award granted, adjusted for changes in the fair value of the referenced investments that employees select.

items.text: Trade press reports that Morgan Stanley is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027, meaning advisors have to generate that much more revenue to see the same pay next year, and that Morgan Stanley is not introducing retention bonuses as part of its 2027 pay plan.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch are not introducing retention bonuses as part of their 2027 pay plans for advisors... Morgan Stanley is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027, meaning advisors have to generate that much more revenue to see the same pay next year.

items.text: Trade press reports that Morgan Stanley has for years taken a small amount of an advisor's gross revenue, called it deferred compensation, and required advisors to stay for years in order to vest (described as golden handcuffs).
items.quote: Giants like Morgan Stanley for years have taken a small amount of an advisor's gross revenue, called it deferred compensation, and required advisors to stay for years in order to vest.
